    CREATE
OR
ALTER PROCEDURE [dbo].[usp_CustomerAnalytics_Processing] @DataDate DATE = NULL,
                                                                          @ProcessType VARCHAR(20) = 'FULL',
                                                                                       @DebugMode BIT = 0,
                                                                                                        @RetentionPeriodDays INT = 365,
                                                                                                                                   @HighValueThreshold DECIMAL(15, 2) = 5000.00,
                                                                                                                                                       @LoyaltyThreshold INT = 5,
                                                                                                                                                                               @ChurnDays_VeryHigh INT = 180,
                                                                                                                                                                                                         @ChurnDays_High INT = 90,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                               @ChurnDays_Medium INT = 60,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       @ChurnDays_Low INT = 30 AS BEGIN
SET NOCOUNT ON; -- Error handling variables
DECLARE @ErrorMessage NVARCHAR(4000); DECLARE @ErrorSeverity INT; DECLARE @ErrorState INT; DECLARE @ErrorLine INT; DECLARE @ErrorProcedure NVARCHAR(200); -- Processing variables
DECLARE @ProcessStartTime DATETIME2 = GETDATE(); DECLARE @StepStartTime DATETIME2; DECLARE @StepName VARCHAR(100); DECLARE @RowCount INT = 0; -- Set default date if not provided
IF @DataDate IS NULL
SET @DataDate = DATEADD(DAY, -1, CAST(GETDATE() AS DATE)); -- Logging helper table

CREATE TABLE #ProcessLog (LogID INT IDENTITY(1, 1), StepName VARCHAR(100), StartTime DATETIME2, EndTime DATETIME2, RowCount INT, Message VARCHAR(1000)); BEGIN TRY -- Log start

SET @StepName = 'Initialize';
SET @StepStartTime = GETDATE();
INSERT INTO #ProcessLog (StepName, StartTime, RowCount, Message)
VALUES (@StepName, @StepStartTime, 0, 'Starting Customer Analytics processing for date: ' + CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), @DataDate, 120) + ' - Type: ' + @ProcessType); -- Temporary tables for processing
 IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#CustomerBase') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #CustomerBase; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#TransactionSummary') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #TransactionSummary; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#CustomerMetrics') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #CustomerMetrics; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#CustomerSegments') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #CustomerSegments; -- Step 1: Extract base customer data
 SET @StepName = 'Extract Customer Base'; SET @StepStartTime = GETDATE(); CREATE TABLE #CustomerBase (CustomerID INT, CustomerName NVARCHAR(100), Email NVARCHAR(200), Phone VARCHAR(20), Address NVARCHAR(500), PostalCode VARCHAR(10), City NVARCHAR(100), State NVARCHAR(100), Country NVARCHAR(100), CustomerType VARCHAR(20), AccountManager INT, CreatedDate DATE, ModifiedDate DATE, IsActive BIT, LastContactDate DATE); -- Create index for better performance
 CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX IX_CustomerBase_CustomerID ON #CustomerBase(CustomerID); INSERT INTO #CustomerBase SELECT c.CustomerID, c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName AS CustomerName, c.Email, c.Phone, a.StreetAddress, a.PostalCode, a.City, a.State, a.Country, c.CustomerType, c.AccountManagerID, c.CreatedDate, c.ModifiedDate, CASE WHEN c.Status = 'Active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS IsActive, MAX(i.ContactDate) AS LastContactDate FROM dbo.Customers c LEFT JOIN dbo.CustomerAddresses a ON c.CustomerID = a.CustomerID AND a.AddressType = 'Primary' LEFT JOIN dbo.CustomerInteractions i ON c.CustomerID = i.CustomerID WHERE (@ProcessType = 'FULL' OR c.ModifiedDate >= @DataDate OR i.ContactDate >= @DataDate) GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName, c.Email, c.Phone, a.StreetAddress, a.PostalCode, a.City, a.State, a.Country, c.CustomerType, c.AccountManagerID, c.CreatedDate, c.ModifiedDate, c.Status; SET @RowCount = @@ROWCOUNT; UPDATE #ProcessLog SET EndTime = GETDATE(), RowCount = @RowCount, Message = 'Extracted base customer data' WHERE StepName = @StepName; -- Step 2: Process Transaction Summary
 SET @StepName = 'Process Transaction Summary'; SET @StepStartTime = GETDATE(); INSERT INTO #ProcessLog (StepName, StartTime, RowCount, Message) VALUES (@StepName, @StepStartTime, 0, 'Calculating transaction metrics'); CREATE TABLE #TransactionSummary (CustomerID INT, TotalOrders INT, TotalSpent DECIMAL(15,2), AvgOrderValue DECIMAL(15,2), FirstPurchaseDate DATE, LastPurchaseDate DATE, DaysSinceLastPurchase INT, TopCategory VARCHAR(50), TopProduct VARCHAR(100), ReturnRate DECIMAL(5,2)); -- Create index for better performance
 CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX IX_TransactionSummary_CustomerID ON #TransactionSummary(CustomerID); -- First, calculate base order metrics
 WITH OrderSummary AS (SELECT o.CustomerID, COUNT(DISTINCT o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders, SUM(od.Quantity * od.UnitPrice * (1 - od.Discount)) AS TotalSpent, MIN(o.OrderDate) AS FirstPurchaseDate, MAX(o.OrderDate) AS LastPurchaseDate FROM dbo.Orders o JOIN dbo.OrderDetails od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID WHERE o.Status = 'Completed' GROUP BY o.CustomerID) SELECT os.CustomerID, os.TotalOrders, os.TotalSpent, CASE WHEN os.TotalOrders > 0 THEN os.TotalSpent / os.TotalOrders ELSE 0 END AS AvgOrderValue, os.FirstPurchaseDate, os.LastPurchaseDate, DATEDIFF(DAY, os.LastPurchaseDate, @DataDate) AS DaysSinceLastPurchase, NULL AS TopCategory,

                                                                                                                                                        -- Will update later
 NULL AS TopProduct, -- Will update later
 0 AS ReturnRate -- Will update later
 INTO #TempOrderSummary FROM OrderSummary os WHERE os.CustomerID IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM #CustomerBase); -- Create index for the temp table
 CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX IX_TempOrderSummary_CustomerID ON #TempOrderSummary(CustomerID); -- Now insert the initial data into transaction summary
 INSERT INTO #TransactionSummary SELECT * FROM #TempOrderSummary; -- Update top category
 WITH ProductCategories AS (SELECT o.CustomerID, p.Category, SUM(od.Quantity * od.UnitPrice * (1 - od.Discount)) AS CategorySpend, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.CustomerID ORDER BY SUM(od.Quantity * od.UnitPrice * (1 - od.Discount)) DESC) AS CategoryRank FROM dbo.Orders o JOIN dbo.OrderDetails od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN dbo.Products p ON od.ProductID = p.ProductID WHERE o.Status = 'Completed' GROUP BY o.CustomerID, p.Category) UPDATE ts SET ts.TopCategory = pc.Category FROM #TransactionSummary ts JOIN ProductCategories pc ON ts.CustomerID = pc.CustomerID AND pc.CategoryRank = 1; -- Update top product
 WITH TopProducts AS (SELECT o.CustomerID, p.ProductName, SUM(od.Quantity) AS TotalQuantity, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.CustomerID ORDER BY SUM(od.Quantity) DESC) AS ProductRank FROM dbo.Orders o JOIN dbo.OrderDetails od ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN dbo.Products p ON od.ProductID = p.ProductID WHERE o.Status = 'Completed' GROUP BY o.CustomerID, p.ProductName) UPDATE ts SET ts.TopProduct = tp.ProductName FROM #TransactionSummary ts JOIN TopProducts tp ON ts.CustomerID = tp.CustomerID AND tp.ProductRank = 1; -- Update return rate
 WITH RETURNS AS (SELECT r.CustomerID, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReturnID) AS TotalReturns, tos.TotalOrders, CASE WHEN tos.TotalOrders > 0 THEN CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReturnID) AS DECIMAL(5,2)) / CAST(tos.TotalOrders AS DECIMAL(5,2)) * 100 ELSE 0 END AS ReturnRate FROM dbo.Returns r JOIN #TempOrderSummary tos ON r.CustomerID = tos.CustomerID GROUP BY r.CustomerID, tos.TotalOrders) UPDATE ts SET ts.ReturnRate = r.ReturnRate FROM #TransactionSummary ts JOIN RETURNS r ON ts.CustomerID = r.CustomerID; -- Drop the temporary table now that we're done with it
 DROP TABLE #TempOrderSummary; SET @RowCount = @@ROWCOUNT; UPDATE #ProcessLog SET EndTime = GETDATE(), RowCount = @RowCount, Message = 'Calculated transaction summary metrics' WHERE StepName = @StepName; -- Step 3: Customer Metrics Calculation
 SET @StepName = 'Calculate Customer Metrics'; SET @StepStartTime = GETDATE(); INSERT INTO #ProcessLog (StepName, StartTime, RowCount, Message) VALUES (@StepName, @StepStartTime, 0, 'Calculating advanced customer metrics'); CREATE TABLE #CustomerMetrics (CustomerID INT, CustomerLifetimeValue DECIMAL(15,2), RecencyScore INT, FrequencyScore INT, MonetaryScore INT, RFMScore INT, ChurnProbability DECIMAL(5,2), NextPurchasePropensity DECIMAL(5,2), LoyaltyIndex DECIMAL(5,2), CustomerHealth VARCHAR(20)); -- Create index for better performance
 CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX IX_CustomerMetrics_CustomerID ON #CustomerMetrics(CustomerID); -- First calculate RFM scores
 WITH RFMScores AS (SELECT ts.CustomerID, -- Recency: 5 is most recent
 NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY ISNULL(ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase, 999999) ASC) AS RecencyScore, -- Frequency: 5 is most frequent
 NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY ISNULL(ts.TotalOrders, 0) DESC) AS FrequencyScore, -- Monetary: 5 is highest value
 NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY ISNULL(ts.TotalSpent, 0) DESC) AS MonetaryScore FROM #TransactionSummary ts) SELECT rfm.CustomerID, rfm.RecencyScore, rfm.FrequencyScore, rfm.MonetaryScore, (rfm.RecencyScore + rfm.FrequencyScore + rfm.MonetaryScore) AS RFMScore INTO #TempRFM FROM RFMScores rfm; -- Create index for the temp table
 CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX IX_TempRFM_CustomerID ON #TempRFM(CustomerID); -- Now calculate churn probabilities and other metrics
 WITH ChurnCalculation AS (SELECT ts.CustomerID, -- Churn probability based on configurable parameters
 CASE WHEN ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase > @ChurnDays_VeryHigh THEN 0.8 WHEN ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase > @ChurnDays_High THEN 0.5 WHEN ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase > @ChurnDays_Medium THEN 0.3 WHEN ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase > @ChurnDays_Low THEN 0.1 ELSE 0.05 END AS ChurnProbability, -- Next purchase propensity
 CASE WHEN ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase < @ChurnDays_Low AND ts.TotalOrders > 3 THEN 0.8 WHEN ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase < @ChurnDays_Medium AND ts.TotalOrders > 2 THEN 0.6 WHEN ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase < @ChurnDays_High THEN 0.4 ELSE 0.2 END AS NextPurchasePropensity, -- Loyalty index - a normalized score (0-1) based on order count and return rate
 CASE WHEN ts.TotalOrders >= @LoyaltyThreshold AND ts.ReturnRate < 10 THEN (ts.TotalOrders * 0.6) + ((100 - ts.ReturnRate) * 0.4) ELSE (ts.TotalOrders * 0.4) END / 10 AS LoyaltyIndex FROM #TransactionSummary ts) INSERT INTO #CustomerMetrics SELECT rfm.CustomerID, 
                 
                                                                                                                                                       -- Customer Lifetime Value (simplified calculation using churn probability)
 ts.TotalSpent * (1 + (1 - ch.ChurnProbability)) AS CustomerLifetimeValue, rfm.RecencyScore, rfm.FrequencyScore, rfm.MonetaryScore, rfm.RFMScore, ch.ChurnProbability, ch.NextPurchasePropensity, ch.LoyaltyIndex, -- Customer Health derived from metrics
 CASE WHEN ch.ChurnProbability > 0.7 THEN 'At Risk' WHEN ch.LoyaltyIndex > 0.8 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN ch.LoyaltyIndex > 0.6 THEN 'Good' WHEN ch.LoyaltyIndex > 0.4 THEN 'Average' ELSE 'Needs Attention' END AS CustomerHealth FROM #TempRFM rfm JOIN #TransactionSummary ts ON rfm.CustomerID = ts.CustomerID JOIN ChurnCalculation ch ON rfm.CustomerID = ch.CustomerID; -- Drop the temporary RFM table now that we're done with it
 DROP TABLE #TempRFM; SET @RowCount = @@ROWCOUNT; UPDATE #ProcessLog SET EndTime = GETDATE(), RowCount = @RowCount, Message = 'Calculated advanced customer metrics' WHERE StepName = @StepName; -- Step 4: Customer Segmentation
 SET @StepName = 'Customer Segmentation'; SET @StepStartTime = GETDATE(); INSERT INTO #ProcessLog (StepName, StartTime, RowCount, Message) VALUES (@StepName, @StepStartTime, 0, 'Performing customer segmentation'); CREATE TABLE #CustomerSegments (CustomerID INT, ValueSegment VARCHAR(50), BehaviorSegment VARCHAR(50), LifecycleSegment VARCHAR(50), TargetGroup VARCHAR(50), MarketingRecommendation VARCHAR(MAX)); -- Create index for better performance
 CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX IX_CustomerSegments_CustomerID ON #CustomerSegments(CustomerID); -- Insert into segments table
 INSERT INTO #CustomerSegments SELECT cb.CustomerID,
                                                                                                                                                  -- Value Segmentation
 CASE WHEN cm.CustomerLifetimeValue >= @HighValueThreshold THEN 'High Value' WHEN cm.CustomerLifetimeValue >= @HighValueThreshold * 0.5 THEN 'Medium Value' ELSE 'Low Value' END AS ValueSegment, -- Behavior Segmentation
 CASE WHEN cm.RFMScore >= 13 THEN 'Champions' WHEN cm.RecencyScore >= 4 AND cm.FrequencyScore >= 3 THEN 'Loyal Customers' WHEN cm.RecencyScore >= 4 AND cm.FrequencyScore <= 2 THEN 'Potential Loyalists' WHEN cm.RecencyScore <= 2 AND cm.FrequencyScore >= 3 AND cm.MonetaryScore >= 3 THEN 'At Risk' WHEN cm.RecencyScore <= 2 AND cm.FrequencyScore <= 2 AND cm.MonetaryScore <= 2 THEN 'Hibernating' WHEN cm.RecencyScore <= 1 THEN 'Lost' ELSE 'Others' END AS BehaviorSegment, -- Lifecycle Segmentation
 CASE WHEN ts.TotalOrders = 1 AND ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase <= 30 THEN 'New Customer' WHEN ts.TotalOrders > 1 AND cm.ChurnProbability < 0.3 THEN 'Active' WHEN cm.ChurnProbability >= 0.3 AND cm.ChurnProbability < 0.7 THEN 'At Risk' WHEN cm.ChurnProbability >= 0.7 THEN 'Churned' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS LifecycleSegment, -- Target Group
 CASE WHEN cm.CustomerLifetimeValue >= @HighValueThreshold AND cm.ChurnProbability < 0.3 THEN 'VIP' WHEN cm.CustomerLifetimeValue >= @HighValueThreshold * 0.5 AND cm.ChurnProbability >= 0.3 THEN 'Retention Priority' WHEN ts.TotalOrders = 1 AND ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase <= 30 THEN 'Nurture New' WHEN cm.NextPurchasePropensity > 0.6 THEN 'Growth Opportunity' WHEN ts.ReturnRate > 20 THEN 'Service Improvement' ELSE 'Standard' END AS TargetGroup, -- Marketing Recommendation
 CASE WHEN cm.CustomerLifetimeValue >= @HighValueThreshold AND cm.ChurnProbability < 0.3 THEN 'Exclusive offers, VIP events, Personal shopping assistance, Early access to new products' WHEN cm.CustomerLifetimeValue >= @HighValueThreshold * 0.5 AND cm.ChurnProbability >= 0.3 THEN 'Re-engagement campaign, Loyalty rewards, Personalized recommendations based on past purchases' WHEN ts.TotalOrders = 1 AND ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase <= 30 THEN 'Welcome series, Educational content, First purchase follow-up, Category exploration' WHEN cm.NextPurchasePropensity > 0.6 THEN 'Cross-sell/upsell, Bundle offers based on ' + ISNULL(ts.TopCategory, 'preferred category') + ', Category expansion' WHEN ts.ReturnRate > 20 THEN 'Satisfaction survey, Improved product information, Size/fit guides, Service recovery' ELSE 'Standard seasonal promotions, Category newsletters, Reactivation after ' + CAST(ISNULL(ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase, 0) / 30 AS VARCHAR) + ' months' END AS MarketingRecommendation FROM #CustomerBase cb JOIN #CustomerMetrics cm ON cb.CustomerID = cm.CustomerID JOIN #TransactionSummary ts ON cb.CustomerID = ts.CustomerID; SET @RowCount = @@ROWCOUNT; UPDATE #ProcessLog SET EndTime = GETDATE(), RowCount = @RowCount, Message = 'Completed customer segmentation' WHERE StepName = @StepName; -- Step 5: Insert into target tables
 SET @StepName = 'Data Persistence'; SET @StepStartTime = GETDATE(); INSERT INTO #ProcessLog (StepName, StartTime, RowCount, Message) VALUES (@StepName, @StepStartTime, 0, 'Persisting data to target tables'); -- Set the isolation level explicitly for data modifications
 SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED; -- Customer Profile table update - using batching for improved performance
 DECLARE @BatchSize INT = 10000; DECLARE @BatchCount INT = 0; DECLARE @TotalCustomers INT = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #CustomerBase); DECLARE @LastCustomerID INT = 0; WHILE @BatchCount < @TotalCustomers BEGIN BEGIN TRANSACTION; -- MERGE statement for Customer Profile (batched)

MERGE INTO dbo.CustomerProfiles AS target USING
  (SELECT TOP (@BatchSize) cb.CustomerID,
          cb.CustomerName,
          cb.Email,
          cb.Phone,
          cb.Address,
          cb.PostalCode,
          cb.City,
          cb.State,
          cb.Country,
          cb.CustomerType,
          cb.AccountManager,
          cb.CreatedDate,
          cb.IsActive,
          cb.LastContactDate,
          ts.TotalOrders,
          ts.TotalSpent,
          ts.AvgOrderValue,
          ts.FirstPurchaseDate,
          ts.LastPurchaseDate,
          ts.DaysSinceLastPurchase,
          ts.TopCategory,
          ts.TopProduct,
          ts.ReturnRate
   FROM #CustomerBase cb
   LEFT JOIN #TransactionSummary ts ON cb.CustomerID = ts.CustomerID
   WHERE cb.CustomerID > @LastCustomerID
   ORDER BY cb.CustomerID) AS SOURCE ON (target.CustomerID = source.CustomerID) WHEN MATCHED THEN
UPDATE
SET target.CustomerName = source.CustomerName,
    target.Email = source.Email,
    target.Phone = source.Phone,
    target.Address = source.Address,
    target.PostalCode = source.PostalCode,
    target.City = source.City,
    target.State = source.State,
    target.Country = source.Country,
    target.CustomerType = source.CustomerType,
    target.AccountManager = source.AccountManager,
    target.IsActive = source.IsActive,
    target.LastContactDate = source.LastContactDate,
    target.TotalOrders = source.TotalOrders,
    target.TotalSpent = source.TotalSpent,
    target.AvgOrderValue = source.AvgOrderValue,
    target.FirstPurchaseDate = source.FirstPurchaseDate,
    target.LastPurchaseDate = source.LastPurchaseDate,
    target.DaysSinceLastPurchase = source.DaysSinceLastPurchase,
    target.TopCategory = source.TopCategory,
    target.TopProduct = source.TopProduct,
    target.ReturnRate = source.ReturnRate,
    target.ModifiedDate = GETDATE() WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
INSERT (CustomerID,
        CustomerName,
        Email,
        Phone,
        Address,
        PostalCode,
        City,
        State,
        Country,
        CustomerType,
        AccountManager,
        CreatedDate,
        IsActive,
        LastContactDate,
        TotalOrders,
        TotalSpent,
        AvgOrderValue,
        FirstPurchaseDate,
        LastPurchaseDate,
        DaysSinceLastPurchase,
        TopCategory,
        TopProduct,
        ReturnRate,
        ModifiedDate)
VALUES (source.CustomerID,
        source.CustomerName,
        source.Email,
        source.Phone,
        source.Address,
        source.PostalCode,
        source.City,
        source.State,
        source.Country,
        source.CustomerType,
        source.AccountManager,
        source.CreatedDate,
        source.IsActive,
        source.LastContactDate,
        source.TotalOrders,
        source.TotalSpent,
        source.AvgOrderValue,
        source.FirstPurchaseDate,
        source.LastPurchaseDate,
        source.DaysSinceLastPurchase,
        source.TopCategory,
        source.TopProduct,
        source.ReturnRate,
        GETDATE());
SET @LastCustomerID =
  (SELECT MAX(CustomerID)
   FROM #CustomerBase
   WHERE CustomerID > @LastCustomerID
     AND CustomerID <= @LastCustomerID + @BatchSize);
SET @BatchCount = @BatchCount + @@ROWCOUNT;
COMMIT TRANSACTION; END -- Customer Analytics table update - replace data for the date (also batched)
 -- First delete existing records for this date
 BEGIN TRANSACTION;
DELETE
FROM dbo.CustomerAnalytics
WHERE ProcessDate = @DataDate;
  COMMIT TRANSACTION; -- Now insert in batches

  SET @BatchCount = 0;
  SET @LastCustomerID = 0; WHILE @BatchCount < @TotalCustomers BEGIN BEGIN TRANSACTION;
  INSERT INTO dbo.CustomerAnalytics (ProcessDate, CustomerID, CustomerLifetimeValue, RecencyScore, FrequencyScore, MonetaryScore, RFMScore, ChurnProbability, NextPurchasePropensity, LoyaltyIndex, CustomerHealth, ValueSegment, BehaviorSegment, LifecycleSegment, TargetGroup, MarketingRecommendation)
  SELECT TOP (@BatchSize) @DataDate,
         cm.CustomerID,
         cm.CustomerLifetimeValue,
         cm.RecencyScore,
         cm.FrequencyScore,
         cm.MonetaryScore,
         cm.RFMScore,
         cm.ChurnProbability,
         cm.NextPurchasePropensity,
         cm.LoyaltyIndex,
         cm.CustomerHealth,
         cs.ValueSegment,
         cs.BehaviorSegment,
         cs.LifecycleSegment,
         cs.TargetGroup,
         cs.MarketingRecommendation
  FROM #CustomerMetrics cm
  JOIN #CustomerSegments cs ON cm.CustomerID = cs.CustomerID
  WHERE cm.CustomerID > @LastCustomerID
  ORDER BY cm.CustomerID;
  SET @RowCount = @@ROWCOUNT;
  SET @BatchCount = @BatchCount + @RowCount;
  SET @LastCustomerID =
    (SELECT MAX(CustomerID)
     FROM #CustomerMetrics
     WHERE CustomerID > @LastCustomerID
       AND CustomerID <= @LastCustomerID + @BatchSize);
  COMMIT TRANSACTION; END -- Cleanup data older than retention period
 IF @DebugMode = 0 BEGIN BEGIN TRANSACTION;
  DELETE
  FROM dbo.CustomerAnalytics
  WHERE ProcessDate < DATEADD(DAY, -@RetentionPeriodDays, @DataDate);
    COMMIT TRANSACTION; END
  UPDATE #ProcessLog
  SET EndTime = GETDATE(),
      RowCount = @BatchCount,
      Message = 'Data persistence completed'
  WHERE StepName = @StepName; -- Step 6: Generate summary report

    SET @StepName = 'Generate Summary';
    SET @StepStartTime = GETDATE();
    INSERT INTO #ProcessLog (StepName, StartTime, RowCount, Message)
  VALUES (@StepName,
          @StepStartTime,
          0,
          'Generating summary statistics'); -- Insert into summary log
 BEGIN TRANSACTION;
  INSERT INTO dbo.CustomerAnalyticsSummary (ProcessDate, ProcessType, TotalCustomers, ActiveCustomers, NewCustomers, ChurningCustomers, HighValueCustomers, AverageLifetimeValue, TotalProcessingTimeMs, ProcessingStatus)
  SELECT @DataDate,
         @ProcessType,
         COUNT(DISTINCT cb.CustomerID),
         SUM(CASE
                 WHEN cs.LifecycleSegment = 'Active' THEN 1
                 ELSE 0
             END),
         SUM(CASE
                 WHEN cs.LifecycleSegment = 'New Customer' THEN 1
                 ELSE 0
             END),
         SUM(CASE
                 WHEN cs.LifecycleSegment = 'At Risk'
                      OR cs.LifecycleSegment = 'Churned' THEN 1
                 ELSE 0
             END),
         SUM(CASE
                 WHEN cs.ValueSegment = 'High Value' THEN 1
                 ELSE 0
             END),
         AVG(cm.CustomerLifetimeValue),
         DATEDIFF(MILLISECOND, @ProcessStartTime, GETDATE()),
         'Success'
  FROM #CustomerBase cb
  JOIN #CustomerMetrics cm ON cb.CustomerID = cm.CustomerID
  JOIN #CustomerSegments cs ON cb.CustomerID = cs.CustomerID;
  SET @RowCount = @@ROWCOUNT;
  COMMIT TRANSACTION;
  UPDATE #ProcessLog
  SET EndTime = GETDATE(),
      RowCount = @RowCount,
      Message = 'Summary statistics generated'
  WHERE StepName = @StepName; -- Log all process steps for debugging
 IF @DebugMode = 1 BEGIN
    SELECT *
    FROM #ProcessLog
    ORDER BY LogID; END -- Cleanup temporary tables
 IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#CustomerBase') IS NOT NULL
    DROP TABLE #CustomerBase; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#TransactionSummary') IS NOT NULL
    DROP TABLE #TransactionSummary; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#CustomerMetrics') IS NOT NULL
    DROP TABLE #CustomerMetrics; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#CustomerSegments') IS NOT NULL
    DROP TABLE #CustomerSegments; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#TempOrderSummary') IS NOT NULL
    DROP TABLE #TempOrderSummary; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#TempRFM') IS NOT NULL
    DROP TABLE #TempRFM; END TRY BEGIN CATCH -- Error handling

  SELECT @ErrorMessage = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
         @ErrorSeverity = ERROR_SEVERITY(),
         @ErrorState = ERROR_STATE(),
         @ErrorLine = ERROR_LINE(),
         @ErrorProcedure = ERROR_PROCEDURE(); -- Rollback any open transaction
 IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0
  ROLLBACK TRANSACTION; -- Log error to process log if it still exists
 IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#ProcessLog') IS NOT NULL BEGIN
  INSERT INTO #ProcessLog (StepName, StartTime, EndTime, RowCount, Message)
  VALUES (@StepName,
          @StepStartTime,
          GETDATE(),
          -1,
          'ERROR: ' + @ErrorMessage); END -- Insert error record into summary

  INSERT INTO dbo.CustomerAnalyticsSummary (ProcessDate, ProcessType, TotalCustomers, TotalProcessingTimeMs, ProcessingStatus, ErrorMessage)
  VALUES (@DataDate,
          @ProcessType,
          0,
          DATEDIFF(MILLISECOND, @ProcessStartTime, GETDATE()),
          'Failed',
          @ErrorMessage + ' at line ' + CAST(@ErrorLine AS VARCHAR(10))); -- Output for debugging
 IF @DebugMode = 1
  AND OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#ProcessLog') IS NOT NULL BEGIN
  SELECT *
  FROM #ProcessLog
  ORDER BY LogID; END -- Cleanup temporary tables before exiting - check if each exists first
 IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#CustomerBase') IS NOT NULL
  DROP TABLE #CustomerBase; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#TransactionSummary') IS NOT NULL
  DROP TABLE #TransactionSummary; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#CustomerMetrics') IS NOT NULL
  DROP TABLE #CustomerMetrics; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#CustomerSegments') IS NOT NULL
  DROP TABLE #CustomerSegments; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#TempOrderSummary') IS NOT NULL
  DROP TABLE #TempOrderSummary; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#TempRFM') IS NOT NULL
  DROP TABLE #TempRFM; IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#ProcessLog') IS NOT NULL
  DROP TABLE #ProcessLog; -- Rethrow the error
 RAISERROR(@ErrorMessage, @ErrorSeverity, @ErrorState); END CATCH; END;

Below is a comprehensive migration plan, along with example PySpark code and testing guidelines for moving the given SQL stored procedure into a Lakehouse environment on Microsoft Fabric, following the medallion architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold). This response is structured to address each role’s perspective and deliverables, focusing on the business logic and how it translates into the new architecture.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. BusinessAnalyst Perspective: Business Analysis
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1.1 Business Purpose and Objectives
• The stored procedure “usp_CustomerAnalytics_Processing” is designed to create a unified customer analytics pipeline.  
• It integrates customer information, transaction summaries, and advanced metrics (RFM, churn probability, loyalty scores).  
• It produces segmented insights, writes data to final analytical tables, and generates summary statistics about process success.  

1.2 Key Business Metrics Calculated
• Customer RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) scores for segmentation.  
• Churn probability based on how many days have passed since last purchase (configurable via @ChurnDays_xxx).  
• Loyalty index (0–1 scale) that uses the number of orders and the product return rate.  
• Customer Lifetime Value (simplified formula multiplying total spent by (1 + (1 – churnProbability))).  
• Customer Segments: Value (“High”, “Medium”, “Low”), Behavior (“Champions”, “Loyal Customers”, etc.), Lifecycle (“New”, “Active”, “At Risk”, “Churned”), plus recommended marketing strategies.  

1.3 Data Sources and Business Context
• “dbo.Customers”, “dbo.CustomerInteractions”, “dbo.CustomerAddresses” for the base customer data.  
• “dbo.Orders”, “dbo.OrderDetails” for transactional data.  
• “dbo.Products”, “dbo.Returns” for product categories, returned orders.  
• Target tables:  
  – “dbo.CustomerProfiles” stores an enriched customer profile with aggregated transaction metrics.  
  – “dbo.CustomerAnalytics” stores advanced metrics (RFM, churn, segmentation).  
  – “dbo.CustomerAnalyticsSummary” tracks daily or incremental aggregates (e.g., totals, new customers, churning customers).  

1.4 Business Rules and Logic
• Allows “FULL” load or incremental loads based on @ProcessType.  
• If @DataDate is null, uses yesterday’s date.  
• Retains historical analytics records for @RetentionPeriodDays (default 365). Older records are purged.  
• RFM scores are computed using standard quintile logic.  
• Churn days thresholds (e.g., 30, 60, 90, 180) are used to compute churn probability tiers.  
• Merges data into “CustomerProfiles” (keeps the latest complete record per customer).  
• Updates the “CustomerAnalytics” table daily (deletes existing day’s data, then inserts the new data).  
• Generates a summary record in “CustomerAnalyticsSummary”.  

1.5 Clear, Non-Technical Explanation
• The procedure collects basic details about customers and their orders.  
• It calculates how often they purchase, how much they spend, and how recently they bought something; these figures feed into RFM scoring.

    .join(cm_silver.alias("cm"), "CustomerID") \

        "CustomerID",
        "FirstName || ' ' || LastName as CustomerName",
        "Email", "Phone",
        "StreetAddress as Address",
        "PostalCode", "City", "State", "Country",
        "CustomerType",
        "AccountManagerID as AccountManager",
        "CreatedDate",
        "ModifiedDate",
        "CASE WHEN Status = 'Active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as IsActive",
        "LastContactDate"
    )
)

# Example incremental logic (pseudo-code):

# else: filter by date or modified fields

cust_base.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/lakehouse/silver/customer_base")

# 2) #TransactionSummary-like DataFrame
orders_join = (
    orders_bronze.alias("o")
    .join(order_details_bronze.alias("od"), col("o.OrderID") == col("od.OrderID"))
    .where(col("o.Status") == lit("Completed"))
)

order_summary = (
    orders_join
    .groupBy("o.CustomerID")
    .agg(
        countDistinct("o.OrderID").alias("TotalOrders"),
        spark_sum(expr("od.Quantity * od.UnitPrice * (1 - od.Discount)")).alias("TotalSpent"),
        spark_min("o.OrderDate").alias("FirstPurchaseDate"),
        spark_max("o.OrderDate").alias("LastPurchaseDate")
    )
)

transaction_summary = (
    order_summary
    .withColumn("AvgOrderValue", when(col("TotalOrders") > 0, col("TotalSpent") / col("TotalOrders")).otherwise(lit(0)))
    .withColumn("DaysSinceLastPurchase", datediff(lit("<DataDate>"), col("LastPurchaseDate")))  # Use real param
)

# Top Category
cat_spend = (
    orders_join
    .join(products_bronze.alias("p"), col("od.ProductID") == col("p.ProductID"))
    .groupBy("o.CustomerID", "p.Category")
    .agg(spark_sum(expr("od.Quantity * od.UnitPrice * (1 - od.Discount)")).alias("CategorySpend"))
)
cat_window = Window.partitionBy("CustomerID").orderBy(col("CategorySpend").desc())
top_category_df = (
    cat_spend
    .withColumn("Rank", row_number().over(cat_window))
    .filter(col("Rank") == 1)
    .select(col("CustomerID"), col("Category").alias("TopCategory"))
)

# Top Product
prod_qty = (
    orders_join
    .join(products_bronze.alias("p"), col("od.ProductID") == col("p.ProductID"))
    .groupBy("o.CustomerID", "p.ProductName")
    .agg(spark_sum("od.Quantity").alias("TotalQuantity"))
)
prod_window = Window.partitionBy("CustomerID").orderBy(col("TotalQuantity").desc())
top_product_df = (
    prod_qty
    .withColumn("Rank", row_number().over(prod_window))
    .filter(col("Rank") == 1)
    .select(col("CustomerID"), col("ProductName").alias("TopProduct"))
)

# Merge top category/product
ts_joined = (
    transaction_summary.alias("ts")
    .join(top_category_df.alias("tc"), "CustomerID", "left")
    .join(top_product_df.alias("tp"), "CustomerID", "left")
    .select("ts.*", "tc.TopCategory", "tp.TopProduct")
)

# ReturnRate
returns_count = returns_bronze.groupBy("CustomerID").agg(countDistinct("ReturnID").alias("TotalReturns"))
ts_with_returns = (
    ts_joined.alias("ts")
    .join(returns_count.alias("r"), "CustomerID", "left")
    .withColumn(
        "ReturnRate",
        when(col("ts.TotalOrders") > 0, (col("r.TotalReturns") / col("ts.TotalOrders")) * 100).otherwise(lit(0))
    )
)

ts_with_returns.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/lakehouse/silver/transaction_summary")

# 3) #CustomerMetrics: RFM, Churn, Loyalty, NextPurchasePropensity, etc.
ts_silver = spark.read.format("delta").load("/lakehouse/silver/transaction_summary")

churn_probability_expr = when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") > 180, lit(0.80)) \
    .when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") > 90, lit(0.50)) \
    .when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") > 60, lit(0.30)) \
    .when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") > 30, lit(0.10)) \
    .otherwise(lit(0.05))

next_purchase_expr = when((col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") < 30) & (col("TotalOrders") > 3), 0.8) \
    .when((col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") < 60) & (col("TotalOrders") > 2), 0.6) \
    .when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") < 90, 0.4) \
    .otherwise(0.2)

loyalty_expr = (
    when((col("TotalOrders") >= lit("<LoyaltyThreshold>")) & (col("ReturnRate") < 10),
         (col("TotalOrders") * 0.6) + ((100 - col("ReturnRate")) * 0.4))
    .otherwise(col("TotalOrders") * 0.4)
) / lit(10)

cust_metrics = (
    ts_silver
    .withColumn("ChurnProbability", churn_probability_expr)
    .withColumn("NextPurchasePropensity", next_purchase_expr)
    .withColumn("LoyaltyIndex", loyalty_expr)
    .withColumn("CustomerLifetimeValue", col("TotalSpent")*(lit(1) + (lit(1) - col("ChurnProbability"))))
    .withColumn(
        "CustomerHealth",
        when(col("ChurnProbability") > 0.7, "At Risk")
        .when(col("LoyaltyIndex") > 0.8, "Excellent")
        .when(col("LoyaltyIndex") > 0.6, "Good")
        .when(col("LoyaltyIndex") > 0.4, "Average")
        .otherwise("Needs Attention")
    )
)

cust_metrics.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/lakehouse/silver/customer_metrics")

# 4) #CustomerSegments
cb_silver = spark.read.format("delta").load("/lakehouse/silver/customer_base")
cm_silver = spark.read.format("delta").load("/lakehouse/silver/customer_metrics")

seg_join = cb_silver.alias("cb").join(cm_silver.alias("cm"), "CustomerID")
customer_segments = (
    seg_join
    .withColumn(
        "ValueSegment",
        when(col("cm.CustomerLifetimeValue") >= lit("<HighValueThreshold>"), "High Value")
        .when(col("cm.CustomerLifetimeValue") >= lit("<HighValueThreshold>") * 0.5, "Medium Value")
        .otherwise("Low Value")
    )
    # Simplified example for BehaviorSegment, LifecycleSegment, etc.

    .withColumn("MarketingRecommendation", lit("..."))
)

customer_segments.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/lakehouse/silver/customer_segments")

----------------------------------
3.3 Gold Layer (Final Tables)
----------------------------------

# Paths for final Delta tables
profiles_path = "/lakehouse/gold/customer_profiles"
analytics_path = "/lakehouse/gold/customer_analytics"
summary_path  = "/lakehouse/gold/customer_analytics_summary"

# 1) Customer Profiles (Mimics the MERGE from #CustomerBase + #TransactionSummary into dbo.CustomerProfiles)

profiles_df = (
    cb_silver.alias("cb")
    .join(ts_silver.alias("ts"), "CustomerID", "left")
    # ... add columns to match the final structure ...
)

if not DeltaTable.isDeltaTable(spark, profiles_path):
    # Initial creation
    profiles_df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(profiles_path)
else:
    # Perform a MERGE to update existing records
    target_profiles = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, profiles_path)
    target_profiles.alias("t").merge(
        profiles_df.alias("s"),
        "t.CustomerID = s.CustomerID"
    ).whenMatchedUpdateAll().whenNotMatchedInsertAll().execute()

# 2) Customer Analytics (Analogous to the daily rebuild in the procedure)
cm_silver = spark.read.format("delta").load("/lakehouse/silver/customer_metrics")
cs_silver = spark.read.format("delta").load("/lakehouse/silver/customer_segments")

analytics_df = (
    cm_silver.alias("cm")
    .join(cs_silver.alias("cs"), "CustomerID")
    .select(
        lit("<DataDate>").alias("ProcessDate"),
        "cm.CustomerID",
        "cm.CustomerLifetimeValue",
        "cm.RecencyScore", "cm.FrequencyScore", "cm.MonetaryScore", "cm.RFMScore",
        "cm.ChurnProbability", "cm.NextPurchasePropensity", "cm.LoyaltyIndex", "cm.CustomerHealth",
        "cs.ValueSegment", "cs.BehaviorSegment", "cs.LifecycleSegment", "cs.TargetGroup", "cs.MarketingRecommendation"
    )
)

if DeltaTable.isDeltaTable(spark, analytics_path):
    target_analytics = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, analytics_path)
    # Delete existing partition/day
    target_analytics.delete("ProcessDate = '<DataDate>'")

analytics_df.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(analytics_path)

# 3) Cleanup older data if retention policy is required
# e.g., 
# target_analytics.delete("ProcessDate < date_sub(current_date, <RetentionPeriodDays>)")

# 4) CustomerAnalyticsSummary
summary_df = (
    cb_silver.alias("cb")
    .join(cm_silver.alias("cm"), "CustomerID")
    .join(cs_silver.alias("cs"), "CustomerID")
    .agg(
        lit("<DataDate>").alias("ProcessDate"),
        lit("<ProcessType>").alias("ProcessType"),
        countDistinct("cb.CustomerID").alias("TotalCustomers"),
        spark_sum(when(col("cs.LifecycleSegment") == "Active", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("ActiveCustomers"),
        spark_sum(when(col("cs.LifecycleSegment") == "New Customer", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("NewCustomers"),
        spark_sum(when((col("cs.LifecycleSegment") == "At Risk") | (col("cs.LifecycleSegment") == "Churned"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("ChurningCustomers"),
        spark_sum(when(col("cs.ValueSegment") == "High Value", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("HighValueCustomers"),
        avg("cm.CustomerLifetimeValue").alias("AverageLifetimeValue")
    )
    .withColumn("TotalProcessingTimeMs", lit(0))  
    .withColumn("ProcessingStatus", lit("Success"))

    summary_df.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(summary_path)
else:
    summary_df.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(summary_path)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. TechLead: Implementation Guidelines & Best Practices
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

4.1 Aligning SQL Transactions with Delta Lake ACID  
• In T-SQL, the stored procedure used BEGIN/COMMIT TRANSACTION blocks. In Spark + Delta Lake, each write/merge operation is already atomic. You typically don’t open a transaction across multiple DataFrame operations.  
• If you need multi-step rollback, consider an orchestration layer or job scheduling approach with checkpoint logic.  

4.2 Error Handling & Logging  
• Replace T-SQL TRY/CATCH blocks and #ProcessLog with a robust logging model:  
  – Use Spark logs, or write process status rows to a “process_logs” Delta table.  
• If a step fails, you can re-run from the last successful state or restore from Delta Lake’s time travel.  

4.3 Performance and Partitioning  
• Partition large tables by date columns (e.g., ProcessDate) to speed up incremental loads and queries.  
• Enable Auto Optimize in Microsoft Fabric for small file management and data compaction.  
• Batch merges or use incremental logic to avoid scanning the entire dataset daily.  

4.4 Scalability  
• Depending on data size, you may scale Spark clusters in Fabric up or down.  
• For “FULL” loads, distributing merges across partitions can improve throughput.  

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. TestingAgent: Test Cases to Validate the Migration
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

5.1 Functional Tests  
• FULL Load Test  
  – Action: Provide a date parameter and set ProcessType=FULL.  
  – Expectation: All relevant data flows through Bronze→Silver→Gold successfully, populating new records.  
• Incremental Load Test  
  – Action: Modify a subset of records in the Bronze area to simulate partial changes.  
  – Expectation: Only changed records are updated; merges in Gold reflect new data.  

5.2 Edge Cases  
• No New or Modified Data  
  – With an incremental run, if no changes occurred since last load, confirm minimal or zero inserts in the Gold tables and no data duplications.  
• Retention Logic  
  – Provide a historical date older than the threshold (e.g., 365 days) and see if the pipeline deletes old partitions or old records.  
• Boundary Churn Days  
  – Ensure recency-based churn calculations (30, 60, 90, 180 days) precisely match the thresholds.  

5.3 Performance & Scale Tests  
• Large Data Volumes  
  – Fill Bronze tables with a heavy volume of customers/orders, confirm the pipeline completes in acceptable time.  
• Stress Testing  
  – Attempt concurrent runs or frequent scheduling to confirm stability and no concurrency conflicts in Delta merges.  

5.4 Data Quality  
• Null or Missing Keys  
  – Confirm how the pipeline handles null CustomerIDs or partially missing data in the Bronze layer.  
• Referenced but Non-Existent Foreign Keys  
  – E.g., an order referencing a ProductID that does not exist in the products table. Validate that the pipeline gracefully excludes or flags such records.  

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Summary and Next Steps  
• You now have a full path to migrate the stored procedure’s logic to Microsoft Fabric’s Lakehouse using PySpark and the medallion architecture.  
• The Bronze layer mirrors raw tables; the Silver layer replicates complex T-SQL transformations; and the Gold layer merges/appends final analytic tables.  
• Replacing T-SQL transaction logic with Delta Lake ACID merges removes the need for manual transaction blocks.  
• By running the recommended tests—functional, edge, performance, and data quality—you can confidently move this pipeline to production and validate its correctness.  

With this plan and code structure, you retain the original business objectives while leveraging the scalability and flexibility of Spark and Delta Lake within Microsoft Fabric.

Below is a comprehensive, end-to-end solution that brings together each stakeholder’s perspective—BusinessAnalyst, ProductOwner, AzureDataEngineer, TechLead, and TestingAgent—to migrate the given SQL stored procedure into Microsoft Fabric using PySpark and a medallion architecture. This includes the overall plan, example PySpark code, best-practice guidelines, and test scenarios.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. BusinessAnalyst Perspective: Requirements & Business Logic
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1.1 Purpose and Summary of the Procedure
• The original T-SQL procedure (usp_CustomerAnalytics_Processing) aggregates and enriches customer data across multiple source tables: Customers, Addresses, Interactions, Orders, OrderDetails, Products, and Returns.  
• It computes advanced metrics like Recency-Frequency-Monetary (RFM) scores, churn probability, loyalty, and segmentation (ValueSegment, BehaviorSegment, LifecycleSegment, TargetGroup), and writes these to final analytics tables.  
• It supports both a full load (ProcessType = 'FULL') or an incremental load (ProcessType = 'INCREMENTAL' or similar value), and cleans up historical data based on a retention period.

1.2 Business Value
• Enables customer segmentation, targeted marketing campaigns, and high-level KPI tracking (e.g., new vs. active, churned customers, average lifetime value).  
• Generates daily or periodic consolidated analytics (CustomerProfiles, CustomerAnalytics, CustomerAnalyticsSummary) for reporting.  
• Integrates a retention mechanism to purge data older than a specified threshold, keeping storage costs under control and ensuring historical data compliance.

1.3 Key Business Metrics
• RFM scoring: Distributes customers into buckets from 1–5 on recency, frequency, and monetary to prioritize.  
• Churn probability: Calculated based on days since last purchase compared to thresholds (e.g., 30, 60, 90, 180).  
• Loyalty index: A 0–1 score using TotalOrders and ReturnRate.  
• Customer lifetime value: A simplified formula multiplying total spent by (1 + (1 – churnProbability)).  
• Segmentation: “High Value,” “Loyal Customers,” “New Customer,” “At Risk,” etc.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. ProductOwner Perspective: Medallion Architecture & Migration Steps
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.1 Medallion Architecture Strategy
• Bronze Layer: Store raw datasets from SQL tables in append-only format in the Lakehouse. No or minimal transformation.  
• Silver Layer: Transform, cleanse, and join data to approximate the logic of the temporary tables (#CustomerBase, #TransactionSummary, #CustomerMetrics, #CustomerSegments).  
• Gold Layer: Present the final analytics tables (CustomerProfiles, CustomerAnalytics, CustomerAnalyticsSummary) that power reporting and BI dashboards.

2.2 Migration Phases
1) Extract & Load to Bronze: Use Microsoft Fabric Dataflows or Spark JDBC to bring SQL tables into Delta files in the Lakehouse.  
2) Transform in Silver:  
   – Build Customer Base (joins of Customers, Addresses, Interactions).  
   – Aggregate orders to form Transaction Summary.  
   – Compute advanced metrics (RFM, churn probability, loyalty scores) in Customer Metrics.  
   – Derive customer segmentation in Customer Segments.  
3) Populate Gold:  
   – Merge or overwrite into CustomerProfiles.  
   – Insert (append) new daily records into CustomerAnalytics.  
   – Generate a daily or incremental record in CustomerAnalyticsSummary.  
   – Optionally prune data older than the retention period.

2.3 Governance and Logging
• Replace T-SQL’s #ProcessLog with a Spark-based or separate Delta-based logging system.  
• Manage data updates via Delta Lake merges or partition-based overwrites.  
• Monitor performance and data quality.  

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. AzureDataEngineer Perspective: PySpark Code (Bronze, Silver, Gold)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Below is example PySpark code illustrating a typical approach. Customize table paths, parameters, thresholds, and scheduling to your environment in Microsoft Fabric:

3.1 Bronze Layer (Raw Ingestion from SQL to Lakehouse)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Connection details (adjust for your environment)

    spark.read.format("jdbc")

         .option("password", db_password)
         .load()

# 2) Write to the Bronze layer in Delta format

3.2 Silver Layer (Transformations & Intermediate Tables)

    when, col, lit, sum as spark_sum, countDistinct, avg, min as spark_min, max as spark_max, expr,
    datediff, row_number
)

addresses_bronze = spark.read.format("delta").load("/lakehouse/bronze/customer_addresses")

# Then join interactions to gather the last contact date

    cust_addr_join
    .join(interactions_bronze.alias("i"), col("c.CustomerID") == col("i.CustomerID"), "left")
    .groupBy(
        "c.CustomerID", "c.FirstName", "c.LastName", "c.Email", "c.Phone",
        "a.StreetAddress", "a.PostalCode", "a.City", "a.State", "a.Country",
        "c.CustomerType", "c.AccountManagerID", "c.CreatedDate", "c.ModifiedDate", "c.Status"

    .selectExpr(

        "PostalCode", "City", "State", "Country",
        "CustomerType",
        "AccountManagerID as AccountManager",
        "CreatedDate",
        "ModifiedDate",

cust_base.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/lakehouse/silver/customer_base")

#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.2.2 #TransactionSummary Equivalent
#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
orders_join = (
    orders_bronze.alias("o")
    .join(order_details_bronze.alias("od"), col("o.OrderID") == col("od.OrderID"))
    .where(col("o.Status") == lit("Completed"))

    countDistinct("o.OrderID").alias("TotalOrders"),
    spark_sum(expr("od.Quantity * od.UnitPrice * (1 - od.Discount)")).alias("TotalSpent"),
    spark_min("o.OrderDate").alias("FirstPurchaseDate"),

)

# Assume <DataDate> is provided as a parameter
DATA_DATE = lit("<DataDate>")  # Replace with actual date param
transaction_summary = (
    order_summary
    .withColumn("AvgOrderValue", when(col("TotalOrders") > 0, col("TotalSpent")/col("TotalOrders")).otherwise(lit(0)))
    .withColumn("DaysSinceLastPurchase", datediff(DATA_DATE, col("LastPurchaseDate")))
)

# Top Category
cat_agg = (
    orders_join
    .join(products_bronze.alias("p"), col("od.ProductID") == col("p.ProductID"))
    .groupBy("o.CustomerID", "p.Category")
    .agg(spark_sum(expr("od.Quantity * od.UnitPrice * (1 - od.Discount)")).alias("CategorySpend"))
)
cat_window = Window.partitionBy("CustomerID").orderBy(col("CategorySpend").desc())
top_category_df = (
    cat_agg
    .withColumn("CategoryRank", row_number().over(cat_window))
    .filter(col("CategoryRank") == 1)
    .select("CustomerID", col("Category").alias("TopCategory"))
)

# Top Product
prod_agg = (
    orders_join
    .join(products_bronze.alias("p"), col("od.ProductID") == col("p.ProductID"))
    .groupBy("o.CustomerID", "p.ProductName")
    .agg(spark_sum("od.Quantity").alias("TotalQuantity"))
)
prod_window = Window.partitionBy("CustomerID").orderBy(col("TotalQuantity").desc())
top_product_df = (
    prod_agg
    .withColumn("ProductRank", row_number().over(prod_window))
    .filter(col("ProductRank") == 1)
    .select("CustomerID", col("ProductName").alias("TopProduct"))
)

# Combine top category/product with transaction summary
ts_with_top = (
    transaction_summary.alias("ts")
    .join(top_category_df.alias("tc"), "CustomerID", "left")
    .join(top_product_df.alias("tp"), "CustomerID", "left")
    .select("ts.*", "tc.TopCategory", "tp.TopProduct")
)

# Return rate
returns_count = returns_bronze.groupBy("CustomerID").agg(countDistinct("ReturnID").alias("TotalReturns"))
ts_with_returns = (
    ts_with_top.alias("ts")
    .join(returns_count.alias("r"), "CustomerID", "left")
    .withColumn(
        "ReturnRate",
        when(col("ts.TotalOrders") > 0, (col("r.TotalReturns")/col("ts.TotalOrders"))*100).otherwise(lit(0))
    )
)

ts_with_returns.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/lakehouse/silver/transaction_summary")

#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.2.3 #CustomerMetrics: RFM, Churn, Loyalty, CLV, etc.
#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ts_silver = spark.read.format("delta").load("/lakehouse/silver/transaction_summary")

# Example threshold parameters from original T-SQL
CHURN_DAYS_VERYHIGH = 180
CHURN_DAYS_HIGH = 90
CHURN_DAYS_MEDIUM = 60
CHURN_DAYS_LOW = 30
LOYALTY_THRESHOLD = 5

churn_probability_expr = (
    when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") > CHURN_DAYS_VERYHIGH, 0.80)
    .when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") > CHURN_DAYS_HIGH, 0.50)
    .when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") > CHURN_DAYS_MEDIUM, 0.30)
    .when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") > CHURN_DAYS_LOW, 0.10)
    .otherwise(0.05)
)

next_purchase_expr = (
    when((col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") < CHURN_DAYS_LOW) & (col("TotalOrders") > 3), 0.8)
    .when((col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") < CHURN_DAYS_MEDIUM) & (col("TotalOrders") > 2), 0.6)
    .when(col("DaysSinceLastPurchase") < CHURN_DAYS_HIGH, 0.4)
    .otherwise(0.2)
)

loyalty_expr = (
    when((col("TotalOrders") >= LOYALTY_THRESHOLD) & (col("ReturnRate") < 10),
         (col("TotalOrders")*0.6) + ((100 - col("ReturnRate"))*0.4))
    .otherwise(col("TotalOrders")*0.4)
) / 10

cust_metrics = (
    ts_silver
    .withColumn("ChurnProbability", churn_probability_expr)
    .withColumn("NextPurchasePropensity", next_purchase_expr)
    .withColumn("LoyaltyIndex", loyalty_expr)
    .withColumn("CustomerLifetimeValue", col("TotalSpent")*(lit(1) + (lit(1) - col("ChurnProbability"))))
    .withColumn(
        "CustomerHealth",
        when(col("ChurnProbability") > 0.7, "At Risk")
        .when(col("LoyaltyIndex") > 0.8, "Excellent")

cust_metrics.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save("/lakehouse/silver/customer_metrics")

#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.2.4 #CustomerSegments
#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4. TechLead Perspective: Implementation Guidelines & Best Practices
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

4.1 Code Quality & Modularity
• Split transformations into smaller, reusable functions or separate notebooks for clarity.  
• Consistently name columns to align with business terms (e.g., “CustomerLifetimeValue” vs. “CLTV”).  

4.2 Performance Considerations
• For large data, partition by relevant columns (e.g., ProcessDate, CustomerID ranges) and enable Auto Optimize in Fabric.  
• Minimize shuffles by reducing unnecessary joins or using broadcast joins for small dimension tables.  
• Use incremental load patterns to avoid scanning the entire dataset daily.  

4.3 Reliability and Logging
• In T-SQL, the stored procedure had a TRY/CATCH with a process log. In PySpark + Delta, one recommended approach is to handle errors in an orchestration tool (like Azure Data Factory or a Fabric pipeline) or write to a “process_logs” table at each step.  
• Delta Lake transactions (MERGE/INSERT) are already atomic, so you don’t need manual BEGIN/COMMIT handling across steps.  

4.4 Governance and Security
• Apply Row-Level Security or other techniques if required in the Power BI or consumption layer.  
• Leverage Azure AD pass-through or Managed Identity for secure data access to SQL sources and the Lakehouse.

5. TestingAgent Perspective: Test Cases & Validation Approach
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

5.1 Functional Tests
• Full Load (ProcessType='FULL'): Confirm that all relevant records flow to the Gold tables.  
• Incremental Load (ProcessType='INCREMENTAL'): Change a small subset of rows in the Bronze layer. Validate that only those rows are recalculated.  

5.2 Edge Cases
• No Data for the Specified Date: Ensure the pipeline gracefully handles an empty or small dataset (should not insert duplicates).  
• Churn Threshold Boundaries: Test exactly 30, 60, 90, 180 days. Confirm correct churn tiers.  
• High Return Rates: Confirm that ReturnRate > 20% triggers relevant remarketing segments.  

5.3 Performance & Scale
• Large Volume: Insert millions of rows to test merges and see if the pipeline completes within acceptable SLAs.  
• Concurrency: If multiple Spark jobs may overlap, confirm no data integrity issues (Delta Lake ACID ensures consistent merges).  

5.4 Data Quality
• Null or Missing Keys: Validate the pipeline handles or filters out incomplete records.  
• Foreign Key Mismatches: For instance, an Order referencing a ProductID not found in Products. Confirm it doesn’t break the pipeline.

Conclusion & Next Steps
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
This plan and sample code show how to replicate the core logic of the T-SQL stored procedure “usp_CustomerAnalytics_Processing” using a medallion architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold) in Microsoft Fabric with PySpark. By following these steps:

• Bronze stores raw data from SQL.  
• Silver applies incremental transformations, aggregations, RFM scoring, and segmentation.  
• Gold merges or appends final analytics tables for reporting.  

Key additional considerations:
• Maintain robust logging for troubleshooting.  
• Tune performance (partitions, cluster sizing, Auto Optimize).  
• Validate end-to-end correctness with the provided test cases.
